Subject: Private offer request: multi-region SKU pooling and reseller margin

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — James and I are ready to move toward a private offer that covers our footprint across AWS, GCP and Azure. A few asks from procurement and our channel partner (MediDist):

- We want SKU pooling across clouds (single private offer covering identical SKUs on AWS/GCP/Azure) so our finance team can report a blended effective unit price. Can Redwood support a blended listprice calculation (usage-weighted) and produce a single invoice path?
- MediDist has requested a reseller margin of 12% on net list. They also want a 2% escrow holdback on first 3 months to ensure proper fulfillment and training. Is that something you can accommodate?
- If a lower reseller margin (10%) requires a commit, tell us what band/commit you’d need.
- Timeline: procurement needs pricing and legal terms to route for approval by end of week.

Attached: Aureon_SKUs_2026.csv (list of SKUs + rough monthly usage).

Can you share a high-level matrix (blended price, reseller margin impact, and whether escrow is supported)?

Best,
Sam Taylor
Head of Procurement
Aureon Health

Subject: Re: Private offer request: multi-region SKU pooling and reseller margin

Hi Sam — appreciate the clarity and the SKU list. Looping in Ben (SalesOps), Jordan (Partner Ops) and Mina (AM) to confirm operational constraints. Quick answers up front:

- SKU pooling: yes — we can create a private offer that maps multiple cloud SKUs into a single offer with a blended listprice. The blended rate will be usage-weighted by the expected monthly consumption you provided. We’ll include per-cloud line items in the offer metadata for billing traces.
- Reseller margin & escrow: our standard reseller pass-through is ~15% list, but we can structure a net 10% margin for MediDist if Aureon signs a minimum 12-month committed ARR (see options below). Escrow is supported operationally as an invoicing holdback; SalesOps needs the PO language and the exact timing (we typically holdbacks funds on our side and remit after verification).

Proposed options (high-level):
1) No commit: maintain 12–15% reseller pass-through. Escrow: not recommended without a commit.
2) 12-month commit of >= $1M ARR: allow 10% reseller margin + 2% escrow for first billing quarter (release after 90 days subject to fulfillment checklist).
3) Higher commit (>= $2M ARR): negotiate to 8% reseller margin with same escrow structure.

Next steps from our side: Ben will run the margin-impact calc and Jordan will confirm invoice routing for MediDist + escrow mechanics. I’ll attach a draft terms PDF with the fallback bands.

Kim / Jordan / Mina — forwarding Aureon’s request and Kimberly’s quick options. I put together a short ops note after a run of the numbers (attached). Key points:

- Blended pricing: straightforward. We build a single private offer with SKU mappings and a blended "effective list" value. Billing will still emit per-cloud line items so accounting can reconcile. No technical blockers.

- Reseller margin impact (rough): if we accept 10% net margin to MediDist, Redwood’s net unit economics worsen by ~8–10% depending on SKU mix; that is sustainable only if we get a firm commit (option 2 above). Without commit, offering <12% materially increases our payback window.

- Escrow mechanics: we can do a 2% escrow on invoice SOV; Redwood will hold that portion and remit to MediDist after 90 days subject to a short fulfillment checklist (training completion + a small usage audit). This requires procurement language and will add a reconciliation step in Finance (we need to tag invoices with escrow flags).

- Required artifacts from Aureon before Ops can finalize: signed MOU or LOI with commit band, expected monthly usage by SKU (you sent this but we’ll need a final version), and MediDist reseller agreement including remit party and taxonomy.

Action items:
- Jordan: confirm invoice flow (direct to Aureon or passthrough to MediDist) and whether MediDist needs to be on the invoice as a cc or separate remit.
- Mina: confirm account team ok to gate the 10% margin on the $1M commit and prepare renewal/rollback language.

I attached: pricing_model_calc.xlsx (tab with scenario math) and a copy of redwood_privoffer_terms_v1.pdf (draft).

Hi Sam / James — thanks for the fast turnaround. Internal ops validated the path and we can proceed on the following agreed framework to get procurement moving:

What Redwood will provide
- A single private offer that pools SKUs across AWS, GCP and Azure with a usage-weighted blended list price. Invoices will include per-cloud line item metadata for auditability.
- Reseller margin structure: 10% net margin to MediDist, contingent on a 12-month committed ARR (>= $1,000,000).
- Escrow: 2% of invoice withheld for the first billing quarter, released after 90 days subject to a short fulfillment checklist (training completion + initial usage verification). Finance will tag and reconcile escrowed amounts.

What we need from Aureon (to finalize legal/ops)
- Signed LOI or MOU that states the commit band (>= $1M ARR) and accept the escrow language.
- Final SKU usage spreadsheet (confirm quantities per cloud) — please replace the provisional CSV with a final XLSX if possible.
- MediDist reseller agreement or remit instructions (who to invoice, tax ID).

Attachments: redwood_privoffer_terms_v1.pdf (draft terms), aureon_pricing_matrix.xlsx (template you can fill), pricing_model_calc.xlsx (ops scenario).

Next steps / timeline
- If Aureon can send the LOI and final SKU file by close of business Thursday (24 Jul), we will prepare the DocuSign package for the private offer and route to Legal for a 24–48 hour review.
- Once signed, SalesOps will provision the private offer in the marketplace (typical lead time 2 business days) and Finance will issue the initial invoice with escrow flags.
